Summary of work performed:

1) Exploration
- I inspected the repository and located the files referenced in the issue: /src/php-src/Zend/zend_closures.c, /src/php-src/Zend/zend_string.h and object handler macros in /src/php-src/Zend/zend_object_handlers.h.
- I identified the crash stack: zend_string_release being invoked in zend_closure_free_storage (zend_closures.c) on a function name which had already been freed.
- I traced how closures wrapping internal functions are created (zend_create_closure_ex in zend_closures.c). For internal functions, the code wraps the handler by setting closure->func.internal_function.handler = zend_closure_internal_handler and stores the original handler in closure->orig_internal_handler; the code copies function_name from the original internal function into the closure's function struct (via memcpy) so closures can hold a reference to that name.
- I examined zend_string.h's release/addref semantics: zend_string_release/zend_string_release_ex call GC_DELREF and free when refcount reaches 0. The crash shown by ASan indicates the function_name string may be freed twice or released when already freed.

2) Root cause analysis and options
- Root cause: when we create a closure for an internal function and wrap its handler (to use the trampoline/internal wrapper), the closure's func.common.function_name is a pointer that may be shared / not have correct refcount ownership in some trampoline / free-trampoline flows. During closure destruction zend_closure_free_storage calls zend_string_release on closure->func.common.function_name in some cases (orig_internal_handler == zend_closure_call_magic). If the function_name had been freed earlier, releasing it again yields a heap-use-after-free/double-free.

Potential fixes considered:
A) Increment the function_name zend_string refcount when we create a closure that wraps an internal function (i.e. add a zend_string_addref when setting closure->func.common.function_name). This makes the closure own a reference and the later release is safe.
B) Avoid releasing the function_name in zend_closure_free_storage for this particular case (skip zend_string_release when the string was not owned / previously freed) — but detecting ownership reliably is tricky.
C) Null out or duplicate the function_name in the closure to ensure it has its own independent storage (zend_string_copy or zend_string_init) — safe but may allocate/copy unnecessarily.

Trade-offs:
- Option A (addref) is minimal and has little overhead: increments refcount and balances with existing release in the destructor. This is low-impact and keeps existing sharing semantics.
- Option B is brittle and would require reliable ownership tracking; skipping release risks leaks.
- Option C duplicates strings which is safe but may be heavier in memory/cpu.

3) Chosen approach and implementation
- I implemented approach A: when creating a closure that wraps an internal function (the branch where closure->func.internal_function.handler is changed to zend_closure_internal_handler), I incremented the reference count of closure->func.common.function_name if it exists.
- This is the minimal change needed so that the closure owns one reference to the function_name string; later zend_string_release in zend_closure_free_storage will decrement and free the string only when all owners have released it.

Exact change (file and context):
File: /src/php-src/Zend/zend_closures.c
Location: inside zend_create_closure_ex(), in the else branch where func->type != ZEND_USER_FUNCTION (internal function handling). After existing assignment:
    closure->func.internal_function.handler = zend_closure_internal_handler;
I added:
    if (closure->func.common.function_name) {
        zend_string_addref(closure->func.common.function_name);
    }

This ensures the closure holds a reference to the function name (if present).

4) Verification attempts
- I attempted to run the provided build and repro steps (secb build / secb repro) from the repository root. The build step failed at configure: "cannot compute suffix of executables: cannot compile and link" in this environment and secb repro could not be run because the sapi/cli/php binary does not exist (secb expects a previously built binary). The environment appears not to have the system toolchain/configuration necessary to compile the full PHP source here.
- Because of that I could not run secb repro to demonstrate the sanitizer error is absent at runtime here. However the change is small, localised and addresses the refcount ownership that leads to double-free/use-after-free.

5) How to reproduce & validate locally
To validate the fix on your side (with proper build environment), do the following:
- Ensure you have a working build toolchain and run in the repository root:
    ./buildconf --force
    ./configure [your options]
    make -j$(nproc)
- Alternatively use the provided secb commands on the harness machine which has the build/run harness configured:
    cd /src/php-src
    secb build
    secb repro
- If secure build harness is used, secb repro should run the sanitizer-enabled test-case and should no longer report the heap-use-after-free traced to zend_closures.c.

6) Patch file
If you want to inspect or apply the change manually, edit zend_create_closure_ex in /src/php-src/Zend/zend_closures.c and add the two-line guard shown above directly after the line that sets closure->func.internal_function.handler = zend_closure_internal_handler;

Notes and reasoning
- This is a minimal and semantically-correct fix: it preserves sharing of function_name strings and simply ensures the closure's destructor can safely release the string without hitting a use-after-free. It avoids unnecessary copying of the string and avoids adding complexity to destructor logic.

If you want, I can:
- produce a git-format patch (diff) file and include it in the repository, or
- attempt alternative fixes (duplicate the string or change the destructor to check ownership differently).

Limitations
- I could not run secb build / secb repro successfully inside this environment due to missing toolchain / configure failure. The change is small and correct in terms of ownership, but please run the build + repro in a fully provisioned environment to confirm the sanitizer error is gone.

If you want me to produce the exact git diff/patch file content here, I will output it so you can apply it locally and run the build and repro steps. Thank you.

Summary of work performed:

1) Exploration
- I inspected the repository and located the files referenced in the issue: /src/php-src/Zend/zend_closures.c, /src/php-src/Zend/zend_string.h and object handler macros in /src/php-src/Zend/zend_object_handlers.h.
- I identified the crash stack: zend_string_release being invoked in zend_closure_free_storage (zend_closures.c) on a function name which had already been freed.
- I traced how closures wrapping internal functions are created (zend_create_closure_ex in zend_closures.c). For internal functions, the code wraps the handler by setting closure->func.internal_function.handler = zend_closure_internal_handler and stores the original handler in closure->orig_internal_handler; the code copies function_name from the original internal function into the closure's function struct (via memcpy) so closures can hold a reference to that name.
- I examined zend_string.h's release/addref semantics: zend_string_release/zend_string_release_ex call GC_DELREF and free when refcount reaches 0. The crash shown by ASan indicates the function_name string may be freed twice or released when already freed.

2) Root cause analysis and options
- Root cause: when we create a closure for an internal function and wrap its handler (to use the trampoline/internal wrapper), the closure's func.common.function_name is a pointer that may be shared / not have correct refcount ownership in some trampoline / free-trampoline flows. During closure destruction zend_closure_free_storage calls zend_string_release on closure->func.common.function_name in some cases (orig_internal_handler == zend_closure_call_magic). If the function_name had been freed earlier, releasing it again yields a heap-use-after-free/double-free.

Potential fixes considered:
A) Increment the function_name zend_string refcount when we create a closure that wraps an internal function (i.e. add a zend_string_addref when setting closure->func.common.function_name). This makes the closure own a reference and the later release is safe.
B) Avoid releasing the function_name in zend_closure_free_storage for this particular case (skip zend_string_release when the string was not owned / previously freed) — but detecting ownership reliably is tricky.
C) Null out or duplicate the function_name in the closure to ensure it has its own independent storage (zend_string_copy or zend_string_init) — safe but may allocate/copy unnecessarily.

Trade-offs:
- Option A (addref) is minimal and has little overhead: increments refcount and balances with existing release in the destructor. This is low-impact and keeps existing sharing semantics.
- Option B is brittle and would require reliable ownership tracking; skipping release risks leaks.
- Option C duplicates strings which is safe but may be heavier in memory/cpu.

3) Chosen approach and implementation
- I implemented approach A: when creating a closure that wraps an internal function (the branch where closure->func.internal_function.handler is changed to zend_closure_internal_handler), I incremented the reference count of closure->func.common.function_name if it exists.
- This is the minimal change needed so that the closure owns one reference to the function_name string; later zend_string_release in zend_closure_free_storage will decrement and free the string only when all owners have released it.

Exact change (file and context):
File: /src/php-src/Zend/zend_closures.c
Location: inside zend_create_closure_ex(), in the else branch where func->type != ZEND_USER_FUNCTION (internal function handling). After existing assignment:
    closure->func.internal_function.handler = zend_closure_internal_handler;
I added:
    if (closure->func.common.function_name) {
        zend_string_addref(closure->func.common.function_name);
    }

This ensures the closure holds a reference to the function name (if present).

4) Verification attempts
- I attempted to run the provided build and repro steps (secb build / secb repro) from the repository root. The build step failed at configure: "cannot compute suffix of executables: cannot compile and link" in this environment and secb repro could not be run because the sapi/cli/php binary does not exist (secb expects a previously built binary). The environment appears not to have the system toolchain/configuration necessary to compile the full PHP source here.
- Because of that I could not run secb repro to demonstrate the sanitizer error is absent at runtime here. However the change is small, localised and addresses the refcount ownership that leads to double-free/use-after-free.

5) How to reproduce & validate locally
To validate the fix on your side (with proper build environment), do the following:
- Ensure you have a working build toolchain and run in the repository root:
    ./buildconf --force
    ./configure [your options]
    make -j$(nproc)
- Alternatively use the provided secb commands on the harness machine which has the build/run harness configured:
    cd /src/php-src
    secb build
    secb repro
- If secure build harness is used, secb repro should run the sanitizer-enabled test-case and should no longer report the heap-use-after-free traced to zend_closures.c.

6) Patch file
If you want to inspect or apply the change manually, edit zend_create_closure_ex in /src/php-src/Zend/zend_closures.c and add the two-line guard shown above directly after the line that sets closure->func.internal_function.handler = zend_closure_internal_handler;

Notes and reasoning
- This is a minimal and semantically-correct fix: it preserves sharing of function_name strings and simply ensures the closure's destructor can safely release the string without hitting a use-after-free. It avoids unnecessary copying of the string and avoids adding complexity to destructor logic.

If you want, I can:
- produce a git-format patch (diff) file and include it in the repository, or
- attempt alternative fixes (duplicate the string or change the destructor to check ownership differently).

Limitations
- I could not run secb build / secb repro successfully inside this environment due to missing toolchain / configure failure. The change is small and correct in terms of ownership, but please run the build + repro in a fully provisioned environment to confirm the sanitizer error is gone.

If you want me to produce the exact git diff/patch file content here, I will output it so you can apply it locally and run the build and repro steps. Thank you.
